survivors.claim: The close-time whole-suite re-run in runCloseTimeGate() does not scrub NODE_TEST_CONTEXT from the child env, contradicting D4's explicit requirement ('with the same env scrub and cwd') and the function's own adjacent comment ('Same env scrub/cwd as the gate re-run above') — the gate re-run two lines above builds a scrubbed `env` local and uses it, but the suite call passes `env: process.env` raw.
survivors.impact: When the driver's own process is invoked from inside a running `node --test` (exactly how this repo's own test suite invokes it via tests/helpers.js runNode, which spawns with the inherited environment), NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is set in that parent process's env. If a host's testCommand runs `node --test`, the unscrubbed child inherits NODE_TEST_CONTEXT and node --test recursively 'skips running files', reporting exit 0 even though the suite is genuinely red — silently defeating the close-time refusal D4 exists to guarantee, for exactly the nested-runner class of host this repo already documents as vulnerable for the gate re-run two lines above.
survivors.evidence: Quoted D4 (spec line 41): 'runs the host `testCommand` bare, after the resolved gate and with the same env scrub and cwd'. Quoted code (spec-review-driver.js:1331-1332 builds `const env = {...process.env}; delete env.NODE_TEST_CONTEXT` and uses it for the gate re-run at line 1333); the suite re-run at line 1354 instead calls `runChild('bash', [...], { cwd: repoRoot, encoding: 'utf8', env: process.env }, ...)` — process.env unscrubbed. Executed repro: `node --test` on a file with NODE_TEST_CONTEXT unset exits 1 on a failing assertion (verified); the same invocation with NODE_TEST_CONTEXT=child-v8 set prints 'Warning: node:test run() is being called recursively within a test file. skipping running files.' and exits 0 despite the failing test (verified via a standalone repro run in this session). Also verified directly: running `node --test tests/review/review-driver.test.js` under this repo prints NODE_TEST_CONTEXT=child-v8 in the test process's own env (confirmed by a throwaway probe test), so tests/helpers.js's runNode (plain spawnSync, no env override) propagates it to any driver child it spawns. AC-20260903-02-10's own test (tests/review/review-driver.test.js) sidesteps this: it uses `testCommand: 'bash always-red.sh'`, a script that fails regardless of NODE_TEST_CONTEXT, so the AC citation does not actually exercise the env-scrub half of D4's promise and the gap is invisible to the suite (all 1048 tests pass with the bug present: `node --test` on this repo at 5588322-plus-diff exits 0, 1048/1048 pass).

killed.claim: review-legs.js's `suite` leg might run concurrently with the gate leg (also a host-test invocation), violating D1's 'never concurrent with another leg that runs host tests'.
killed.evidence: Read the control flow: wave 1 (reconcile/gate/ci) is built into an array `wave1` and run via `await Promise.all(wave1)` (line ~261-279); the suite block (lines 284-305) executes only after that await resolves, sequentially, before wave 2's array is built. AC-20260903-02-6's new test in tests/review/review-legs-smoke-wave.test.js also directly proves ordering (suite-done exists before the at-risk invocation starts) — executed: `node --test tests/review/review-legs-smoke-wave.test.js` passes (confirmed as part of the full-suite green run, 1048/1048).

killed.claim: verdict.js's fix-delta requiredLegs filter might drop `suite` the way it drops `reconcile`/`at-risk`, violating D3's 'required in BOTH scopes'.
killed.evidence: Read the filter: `scope === 'fix-delta' ? REVIEW_LEGS.filter(l => l !== 'reconcile' && l !== 'at-risk') : [...REVIEW_LEGS]` — suite is not named in the filter predicate, so it survives into fix-delta's requiredLegs. AC-20260903-02-3 and the two AC-20260903-02-7 tests (full and fix-delta variants) in tests/review/review-legs.test.js and tests/review/verdict.test.js assert this directly; both pass in the full-suite green run.
